standard.title: Share arts works with audiences
standard.description: share their arts works with audiences
standard.prior_knowledge: No formal prior arts learning assumed. Students bring informal experience with showing things to others (e.g. showing a drawing to a parent). Formal experience of sharing arts works with an audience is new.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students share their arts works with an audience, introduce what the work is about, and respond to questions or comments about it.

nodes.label: What it means to have an audience
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students understand that sharing arts works involves an audience with a role to play — watching, listening and responding.
nodes.minimum_width: Participate as an audience member during a peer sharing: listen or watch quietly, then make one positive comment about what they noticed.
nodes.typical_width: Experience both roles — performer/sharer and audience member; practise using positive language to comment on others' works; understand that the audience's role is to engage with and respond to the work, not just to watch.
wider: Discuss the difference between being an audience at a school performance vs watching a cartoon at home — what does the performer/artist need from each?
Practise responding to an arts work with specific observations (e.g. 'I noticed the chant got faster') rather than only general praise
nodes.hinge_reason: Understanding that performance involves an audience relationship — not just doing something in front of people — is foundational to all presenting and performing work. Students who see sharing as 'showing and sitting down' do not develop the intentional communication of later performance work. This concept underpins AC9AMU2P01's requirements around staging, introduction and post-performance discussion.

response_modes.reason: Explicitly teach the audience role before sharing events: 'When you are the audience, your job is to...' Debrief after sharing: 'What was it like to perform? What was it like to watch?' Build language for responding to arts works.

success_criteria: Participates appropriately as an audience member (watching/listening during the performance)
Can make at least one specific positive comment about another student's work

nodes.label: Introducing and sharing a work
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can introduce their arts work to an audience by naming one feature of it, then perform or display it.
nodes.minimum_width: Before or after sharing, say one thing about their arts work (e.g. 'This is a chant about running' or 'I made this to show my dog').
nodes.typical_width: Introduce works by naming the theme, process or a favourite part; share arts works in at least two formats (e.g. a gallery walk and a performance); respond to teacher questions such as 'What is going on in your work?'
wider: Introduce a performance by telling the audience what you want them to listen for or feel — practise this as a structured sentence before the performance
Take turns as a 'gallery guide' — stand next to their displayed work and explain it to visiting classmates

response_modes.reason: Students need experience sharing works in multiple formats (gallery, performance, digital) so they develop a repertoire of sharing modes. Each format teaches slightly different performance skills — standing and speaking differs from performing a song differs from pointing to a displayed work.

success_criteria: Introduces their arts work with at least one identifying statement before or after sharing
Can respond to one question about their work from the teacher or a peer

nodes.label: Performing with music skills
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can perform a song, soundscape or chant using at least one practised music skill (e.g. matching starting pitch, staying in time with the group, following a simple graphic score).
nodes.minimum_width: Perform a song or chant with the group, demonstrating awareness of at least one music convention (e.g. staying in time, or using singing voice rather than speaking voice).
nodes.typical_width: Perform songs, soundscapes or chants using practised skills — matching pitch, staying in time, following an agreed plan or graphic score; use a digital device to document the performance via images or recording.
wider: Follow a graphic score when performing a soundscape — practise reading the score in rehearsal and apply it in performance
Curate a sequence of digital images from a class arts event and add voice narration or soundscape as commentary

response_modes.reason: Music performance skills at Foundation (staying in time, matching pitch, following an agreed plan) require repeated practice in low-stakes contexts before students can apply them reliably in a shared performance. Fluency here underpins the more deliberate performance decisions required at Y1-2.

success_criteria: Performs a song or chant as part of a group with some awareness of at least one music convention
Attempts to match the group's timing or dynamic level during the performance
